title: I Followed the Letterpress Chase Booking Into the Slot They Left Locked

parts.text: I unlocked chase B at 2:01 p.m. and mentor Hugo's type was still locked in my unpaid-looking leftover. The calendar said: BOOK THE PRESS. NINETY MINUTES. CLEAR THE CHASE. I was thirty, resident, holding a calendar hold. Hugo did not stop. "Mentors are the press." I photographed the calendar, the hold, and his lock on my time. Then I logged an overlap. At 2:08 the studio manager asked why Hugo's chase was on my hold. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio manager can see Hugo's locked type on chase B during my hold.

social.video_title: He left his type locked in my booked chase — Part 1/2
social.description: Letterpress, a calendar hold, and a mentor still locked. I logged the overlap. Would you have knocked?

parts.text: Hugo called it a form until the manager asked for the log. I printed the overlap, the photo, and the hold. He unlocked. Hugo booked his own ninety and told residents forms were always about optics. Optics is a word mentors use when holds exist. Booking now has a second line: MENTORS CLEAR THE CHASE. I keep my ninety. Hugo schedules. The press finally sounds like a hold, not leftover type. I kept the printout in a folder labeled BORING. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Overlap log, unlocked type, and a second line. Was a form ever my hold?
